findings.body: Event creation throws when reading `integration` from `undefined`, so the booking flow fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.
findings.failure_mode: The Meet booking path fails at runtime (and under strict null checking, fails type checking).
findings.impact: Event creation throws when reading `integration` from `undefined`, so the booking flow fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.
findings.root_cause: The array destructuring can yield `undefined`, but the replacement condition accesses its property unconditionally.
findings.suggested_fix: Use optional chaining (for example, `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) or explicitly handle an absent first destination before evaluating the fallback.
findings.title: Avoid dereferencing an absent destination calendar for Meet fallback
findings.trigger: A booking selects Google Meet while its event type and organizer have no destination calendar, leaving `evt.destinationCalendar` null or empty.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 119 exists verbatim in patch. Destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when array is empty, then accessing `.integration` throws TypeError. Trigger is realistic: booking with Meet location but no destination calendar.

findings.body: The optional push is skipped because the initial value is `null`, so the other hosts' destination calendars are never sent to `EventManager` and no events are created for them.
findings.failure_mode: A valid collective host's configured calendar is silently omitted from the booking.
findings.impact: The optional push is skipped because the initial value is `null`, so the other hosts' destination calendars are never sent to `EventManager` and no events are created for them.
findings.root_cause: Collective destinations are appended only if the initially selected primary destination already exists.
findings.suggested_fix: Initialize `destinationCalendar` to an empty array before appending collective-host destinations, or assign `teamDestinationCalendars` when no primary destination exists.
findings.title: Do not drop collective-host calendars when the primary host has none
findings.trigger: A collective event has no event-type destination calendar and the first/organizer host has no destination calendar, while one or more other collective hosts do have one.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 1078 exists verbatim. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (lines 1063-1067 show it can be null), optional chaining `?.push` is a no-op, so `teamDestinationCalendars` are never added. Collective hosts lose their calendars.

findings.body: The organization is created without the requested `slug`, whereas the previous branch stored the slug in this mode. The organization cannot be addressed by its requested slug and downstream slug-based organization behavior receives a missing value.
findings.failure_mode: Organization creation stores incomplete routing identity data in the normal non-team-billing configuration.
findings.impact: The organization is created without the requested `slug`, whereas the previous branch stored the slug in this mode. The organization cannot be addressed by its requested slug and downstream slug-based organization behavior receives a missing value.
findings.root_cause: The team-billing predicate controlling slug assignment was inverted.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the original disabled-billing condition for assigning `slug`; retain the requested-slug metadata behavior for the enabled-billing path.
findings.title: Do not omit organization slugs when team billing is disabled
findings.trigger: An organization is created in an environment where `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 151 exists verbatim. Original was `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }`, now `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. Logic inverted: slug now set only when billing enabled, omitted when disabled. Organizations created without slug in non-billing environments.

pr.body:
## What does this PR do?

- Converts destinationCalendar on CalendarEvent to be an array.
- Patches and fixes so every sentence of code that was using evet.destinationCalendar can support the new type of array.
- The logic here is to fallback to normal behaviour has having one main destinationCalendar but also supports multiple so host can get invited correctly.

Fixes #7754 
## Loom 
Creating event and rescheduling:
https://www.loom.com/share/3cb3af513d274ed2bdfed44e48edddf6?sid=d81ce3de-2893-4a30-b085-ff67c31b7dfb

Canceling event:
https://www.loom.com/share/7ef505d4665e4d4982d2bb2d7b118085?sid=cd43c97c-aa86-4667-979f-f6492adf3365

## Requirement/Documentation

## Type of change

<!-- Please delete bullets that are not relevant. -->

- [X] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## How should this be tested?

- Are there environment variables that should be set? No
- What are the minimal test data to have? Setup a collective event using teampro and teamfree users. Add any app calendar to those accounts and add them as host for collective event.
- What is expected (happy path) to have (input and output)? Collective event with 2 host and every user with any calendar app installed should receive proper calendar events.
- Any other important info that could help to test that PR

## Mandatory Tasks

- [X] Make sure you have self-reviewed the code. A decent size PR without self-review might be rejected.

## Checklist

- I haven't added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works

raw_findings.body: Only the first destination is persisted on the booking. Later handlers reconstruct the calendar event from that singular relation and can create an event only for the primary host, losing the other collective hosts' destinations.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Deferred workflows cannot reproduce the multi-host calendar targets selected at booking time.
raw_findings.impact: Only the first destination is persisted on the booking. Later handlers reconstruct the calendar event from that singular relation and can create an event only for the primary host, losing the other collective hosts' destinations.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new array is reduced to index zero when the booking is stored.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Persist all selected destination calendars in a relation or other durable booking data, and have deferred creation handlers reconstruct the complete destination list.
raw_findings.title: Retain every collective destination for deferred event creation
raw_findings.trigger: A collective booking with multiple destination calendars is initially pending, such as a paid or requires-confirmation booking, and calendar events are created later by a payment or confirmation handler.

raw_findings.body: Every invocation uses the first host's external calendar ID. Later host credentials therefore attempt to create in the first host's calendar, which can fail authorization or create the event in the wrong calendar instead of the corresponding host's calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Collective Lark events are not reliably created in each host's configured calendar.
raw_findings.impact: Every invocation uses the first host's external calendar ID. Later host credentials therefore attempt to create in the first host's calendar, which can fail authorization or create the event in the wrong calendar instead of the corresponding host's calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: The Lark service treats a multi-destination event as though the first destination applies to every credential.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the selected destination/external calendar ID into the service, or select the destination by the active credential ID rather than destructuring index zero.
raw_findings.title: Select the Lark destination that belongs to the credential being used
raw_findings.trigger: A collective booking has Lark destination calendars for multiple hosts and `EventManager` invokes this service once with each host credential.

raw_findings.body: All requests use the first host's calendar ID, so subsequent host credentials can receive authorization errors or create events in the wrong calendar rather than their own destination calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: The multiple-host destination feature does not work for Office 365 calendars.
raw_findings.impact: All requests use the first host's calendar ID, so subsequent host credentials can receive authorization errors or create events in the wrong calendar rather than their own destination calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: Office 365 creation always selects array index zero while event creation iterates multiple credentials.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Provide the selected destination to `createEvent` and construct the URL from that destination, or select the array item using the active credential ID.
raw_findings.title: Select the Office 365 destination that belongs to the credential being used
raw_findings.trigger: A collective booking has Office 365 destination calendars for multiple hosts and event creation runs once per host credential.

raw_findings.body: Each credential filters its available calendars using the first host's external ID. Other hosts' credentials generally do not own that calendar, so their event creation fails or is skipped instead of writing to their selected destination.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Collective events cannot be reliably created across DAV-based host calendars.
raw_findings.impact: Each credential filters its available calendars using the first host's external ID. Other hosts' credentials generally do not own that calendar, so their event creation fails or is skipped instead of writing to their selected destination.
raw_findings.root_cause: The shared DAV service converts the destination array to a single global first destination despite per-host creation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the current destination/calendar ID through the creation call and filter against that destination for each credential rather than the first array element.
raw_findings.title: Do not make DAV calendar creation use only the first collective destination
raw_findings.trigger: A collective booking has multiple DAV/CalDAV host destinations and creation is invoked with credentials for more than one host.

raw_findings.body: `createEvent` receives no `externalId`, so its result produces a booking reference with no `externalCalendarId`. Subsequent updates and deletes cannot identify the destination calendar, and services that depend on the reference may target the wrong calendar.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Calendar references created for legacy destinations lose the information required to address the created event later.
raw_findings.impact: `createEvent` receives no `externalId`, so its result produces a booking reference with no `externalCalendarId`. Subsequent updates and deletes cannot identify the destination calendar, and services that depend on the reference may target the wrong calendar.
raw_findings.root_cause: The no-credential branch discards the destination's external ID while creating calendar events.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Pass `destination.externalId` as the third argument to `createEvent` in this branch, just as the credential-ID branch does.
raw_findings.title: Preserve the selected external calendar for destinations without a credential ID
raw_findings.trigger: A destination calendar has `credentialId: null` (which is permitted by the schema), such as a legacy destination, and there are matching connected calendar credentials.

raw_findings.body: No destination matches the active numeric credential ID, so insertion falls back to `primary` rather than the configured destination calendar. Previously the configured external ID was used regardless of whether a credential ID was stored.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Valid legacy Google destination configurations create events in the account primary calendar rather than the selected calendar.
raw_findings.impact: No destination matches the active numeric credential ID, so insertion falls back to `primary` rather than the configured destination calendar. Previously the configured external ID was used regardless of whether a credential ID was stored.
raw_findings.root_cause: Calendar selection was changed from using the destination external ID to requiring a credential-ID match.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When no credential-ID match exists, fall back to the applicable destination's `externalId` (or pass the selected destination explicitly from `EventManager`).
raw_findings.title: Use the configured Google calendar when its destination has no credential ID
raw_findings.trigger: A Google destination calendar has no `credentialId` but has an `externalId`, and event creation uses a connected Google credential.

raw_findings.body: The insert succeeds on `primary`, but `selectedCalendar` remains `undefined` and is later passed directly to the patch call. The Meet-link description patch fails or is sent with an invalid calendar ID.
raw_findings.failure_mode: New Google Meet events can be created without the expected rich-description update containing the meeting link.
raw_findings.impact: The insert succeeds on `primary`, but `selectedCalendar` remains `undefined` and is later passed directly to the patch call. The Meet-link description patch fails or is sent with an invalid calendar ID.
raw_findings.root_cause: The primary-calendar fallback is applied only at the insert call site, not to the variable reused by the patch call.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Assign the fallback into `selectedCalendar` itself (for example, `const selectedCalendar = matchedExternalId ?? "primary"`) and use that value for both insert and patch.
raw_findings.title: Keep the Google calendar ID valid for the post-create Meet patch
raw_findings.trigger: Google event creation has no credential-matching destination calendar, falls back to `primary`, and Google returns a `hangoutLink` that triggers the subsequent `calendar.events.patch` call.

raw_findings.body: The lookup compares every external ID to `null`/`undefined` and returns no calendar ID. Google update requests therefore receive an undefined `calendarId` instead of falling back to the event's configured destination as before.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Updates for affected bookings fail at the Google Calendar API rather than updating the existing calendar event.
raw_findings.impact: The lookup compares every external ID to `null`/`undefined` and returns no calendar ID. Google update requests therefore receive an undefined `calendarId` instead of falling back to the event's configured destination as before.
raw_findings.root_cause: The single-destination fallback was replaced with a lookup using the absent input value.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When `externalCalendarId` is absent, select the relevant destination (at minimum the first destination for legacy single-destination events) rather than searching for an undefined ID.
raw_findings.title: Fall back to the event destination when a Google update reference lacks an external ID
raw_findings.trigger: An update is performed for a calendar reference with a null or missing `externalCalendarId`, while the `CalendarEvent` still has a destination calendar.

raw_findings.body: The new loop creates multiple calendar references, but the merge cleanup later still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first old calendar event. Old events remain on the other hosts' calendars after rescheduling.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Rescheduling leaves stale events and busy blocks on secondary host calendars.
raw_findings.impact: The new loop creates multiple calendar references, but the merge cleanup later still uses `booking.references.find(...)` and deletes only the first old calendar event. Old events remain on the other hosts' calendars after rescheduling.
raw_findings.root_cause: Creation was expanded to multiple destination references while the reschedule cleanup still assumes one calendar reference.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When `newBookingId` is supplied, filter all old calendar references and delete each with its corresponding credential and external calendar ID.
raw_findings.title: Delete every old calendar event when rescheduling a multi-destination booking
raw_findings.trigger: A multi-destination collective booking is rescheduled through the path that supplies `newBookingId`.

raw_findings.body: For each outer reference, the recurring branch still finds only the first `_calendar` reference on each updated booking and iterates the booking owner's credentials. Secondary host references are not selected for deletion; instead the primary event may be deleted repeatedly while secondary calendar events remain.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Cancelling a recurring collective series leaves orphaned events on secondary hosts' calendars.
raw_findings.impact: For each outer reference, the recurring branch still finds only the first `_calendar` reference on each updated booking and iterates the booking owner's credentials. Secondary host references are not selected for deletion; instead the primary event may be deleted repeatedly while secondary calendar events remain.
raw_findings.root_cause: The cancellation code now iterates multiple references, but its recurring-occurrence branch retains single-reference lookup logic.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: For every updated booking, iterate all calendar references and delete each through its matching credential, rather than using `find` for a single reference inside every outer iteration.
raw_findings.title: Delete secondary recurring-host events instead of repeatedly selecting the first reference
raw_findings.trigger: All remaining occurrences of a recurring collective booking with multiple calendar references are cancelled.

validated_findings.body: Event creation throws when reading `integration` from `undefined`, so the booking flow fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The Meet booking path fails at runtime (and under strict null checking, fails type checking).
validated_findings.impact: Event creation throws when reading `integration` from `undefined`, so the booking flow fails instead of falling back to Cal Video.
validated_findings.root_cause: The array destructuring can yield `undefined`, but the replacement condition accesses its property unconditionally.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Use optional chaining (for example, `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration !== "google_calendar"`) or explicitly handle an absent first destination before evaluating the fallback.
validated_findings.title: Avoid dereferencing an absent destination calendar for Meet fallback
validated_findings.trigger: A booking selects Google Meet while its event type and organizer have no destination calendar, leaving `evt.destinationCalendar` null or empty.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 119 exists verbatim in patch. Destructuring `evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` yields `undefined` when array is empty, then accessing `.integration` throws TypeError. Trigger is realistic: booking with Meet location but no destination calendar.

validated_findings.body: The optional push is skipped because the initial value is `null`, so the other hosts' destination calendars are never sent to `EventManager` and no events are created for them.
validated_findings.failure_mode: A valid collective host's configured calendar is silently omitted from the booking.
validated_findings.impact: The optional push is skipped because the initial value is `null`, so the other hosts' destination calendars are never sent to `EventManager` and no events are created for them.
validated_findings.root_cause: Collective destinations are appended only if the initially selected primary destination already exists.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize `destinationCalendar` to an empty array before appending collective-host destinations, or assign `teamDestinationCalendars` when no primary destination exists.
validated_findings.title: Do not drop collective-host calendars when the primary host has none
validated_findings.trigger: A collective event has no event-type destination calendar and the first/organizer host has no destination calendar, while one or more other collective hosts do have one.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 1078 exists verbatim. When `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` (lines 1063-1067 show it can be null), optional chaining `?.push` is a no-op, so `teamDestinationCalendars` are never added. Collective hosts lose their calendars.

validated_findings.body: Only the first destination is persisted on the booking. Later handlers reconstruct the calendar event from that singular relation and can create an event only for the primary host, losing the other collective hosts' destinations.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Deferred workflows cannot reproduce the multi-host calendar targets selected at booking time.
validated_findings.impact: Only the first destination is persisted on the booking. Later handlers reconstruct the calendar event from that singular relation and can create an event only for the primary host, losing the other collective hosts' destinations.
validated_findings.root_cause: The new array is reduced to index zero when the booking is stored.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Persist all selected destination calendars in a relation or other durable booking data, and have deferred creation handlers reconstruct the complete destination list.
validated_findings.title: Retain every collective destination for deferred event creation
validated_findings.trigger: A collective booking with multiple destination calendars is initially pending, such as a paid or requires-confirmation booking, and calendar events are created later by a payment or confirmation handler.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 1877 exists verbatim showing `connect: { id: evt.destinationCalendar[0].id }`. Only first destination persisted to booking relation. Deferred handlers reconstructing from booking lose other hosts' destinations. Systemic data loss for multi-host bookings.

validated_findings.body: Every invocation uses the first host's external calendar ID. Later host credentials therefore attempt to create in the first host's calendar, which can fail authorization or create the event in the wrong calendar instead of the corresponding host's calendar.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Collective Lark events are not reliably created in each host's configured calendar.
validated_findings.impact: Every invocation uses the first host's external calendar ID. Later host credentials therefore attempt to create in the first host's calendar, which can fail authorization or create the event in the wrong calendar instead of the corresponding host's calendar.
validated_findings.root_cause: The Lark service treats a multi-destination event as though the first destination applies to every credential.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Pass the selected destination/external calendar ID into the service, or select the destination by the active credential ID rather than destructuring index zero.
validated_findings.title: Select the Lark destination that belongs to the credential being used
validated_findings.trigger: A collective booking has Lark destination calendars for multiple hosts and `EventManager` invokes this service once with each host credential.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 128 exists verbatim in LarkCalendarService. Always uses first destination's externalId regardless of which credential is being used. EventManager iterates credentials but Lark service ignores credential context, causing wrong calendar targeting.

validated_findings.body: All requests use the first host's calendar ID, so subsequent host credentials can receive authorization errors or create events in the wrong calendar rather than their own destination calendar.
validated_findings.failure_mode: The multiple-host destination feature does not work for Office 365 calendars.
validated_findings.impact: All requests use the first host's calendar ID, so subsequent host credentials can receive authorization errors or create events in the wrong calendar rather than their own destination calendar.
validated_findings.root_cause: Office 365 creation always selects array index zero while event creation iterates multiple credentials.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Provide the selected destination to `createEvent` and construct the URL from that destination, or select the array item using the active credential ID.
validated_findings.title: Select the Office 365 destination that belongs to the credential being used
validated_findings.trigger: A collective booking has Office 365 destination calendars for multiple hosts and event creation runs once per host credential.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 73 exists verbatim in Office365CalendarService. Same pattern as Lark: always uses first destination regardless of active credential. Multi-host collective bookings will target wrong calendars.

validated_findings.body: The organization is created without the requested `slug`, whereas the previous branch stored the slug in this mode. The organization cannot be addressed by its requested slug and downstream slug-based organization behavior receives a missing value.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Organization creation stores incomplete routing identity data in the normal non-team-billing configuration.

validated_findings.root_cause: The team-billing predicate controlling slug assignment was inverted.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Restore the original disabled-billing condition for assigning `slug`; retain the requested-slug metadata behavior for the enabled-billing path.
validated_findings.title: Do not omit organization slugs when team billing is disabled
validated_findings.trigger: An organization is created in an environment where `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` is false.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Line 151 exists verbatim. Original was `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }`, now `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`. Logic inverted: slug now set only when billing enabled, omitted when disabled. Organizations created without slug in non-billing environments.
